meta.description: Database of proven hooks from high-performing launch videos and content with millions of views. Use these patterns as templates — never copy verbatim.

hook_patterns.pattern: Challenge a widely-held belief with a specific counterexample
hook_patterns.template: Everyone says [common belief]. [Specific person/company] proved them wrong by [specific result].
examples: Everyone says you need a huge team to build a billion-dollar company. This founder did it with 3 people and a script.
Everyone says SEO is dead. This brand got 10M organic visits last month. Here's how.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Triggers cognitive dissonance — the viewer needs to resolve the conflict between what they believe and what you're claiming.

hook_patterns.pattern: Lead with a specific, surprising number that defies expectations
examples: $3.2M in revenue from a single launch video. Here's the 60-second script that did it.
47 seconds. That's how long it takes this tool to do what used to take your team 3 weeks.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Specific numbers create instant credibility and curiosity. The gap between the number and expectations creates an open loop.

hook_patterns.pattern: Open with a specific moment or scenario the audience has lived
hook_patterns.template: You know that moment when [ultra-specific scenario]? [Unexpected twist].
examples: You know that moment when you realize you've been manually doing something that could've been automated 6 months ago? That's how I felt when I found this.
You know that feeling when your best developer quits and takes all the context with them? We built the fix.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Instant relatability. The viewer sees themselves in the scenario and feels understood. The twist creates curiosity.

hook_patterns.pattern: Directly challenge the viewer's current approach
hook_patterns.template: If you're still [common approach], you're [leaving value on the table / falling behind / doing it wrong]. Here's what [smart people / top companies] are doing instead.
examples: If you're still writing launch scripts by yourself, you're leaving millions on the table. Here's what the top 1% of founders do instead.
If you're still using spreadsheets for this, I need to show you something.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Creates fear of being left behind (FOMO) combined with the promise of a better way. The viewer feels personally called out.

hook_patterns.pattern: Position the information as something most people don't know
hook_patterns.template: [X%] of [audience] don't know [surprising fact]. The ones who do are [impressive result].
examples: 97% of founders launch their product wrong. The 3% who don't are averaging 10x more revenue on launch day.
There's a feature in this tool that nobody talks about. It's the reason 4 of our clients hit $1M ARR.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Creates an in-group/out-group dynamic. The viewer wants to be in the group that knows. Exclusivity drives curiosity.
hook_patterns.best_for: Products with non-obvious value or hidden features

hook_patterns.pattern: Lead with the end result, then promise to show how
hook_patterns.template: [Person/Company] [achieved specific result]. [They/I] used [surprising method]. Here's exactly how.
examples: This startup went from $0 to $5M ARR in 8 months. Their secret? A 90-second video and this script framework.
I turned $500 in ad spend into $47,000 in revenue. Not with a funnel. With a single video.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: The result creates desire. The surprising method creates curiosity. 'Here's how' creates an open loop that requires watching to close.

hook_patterns.pattern: Compare old way vs new way with shocking specificity
hook_patterns.template: [Old way]: [painful specific]. [New way]: [impressive specific]. Same [task/goal]. [Fraction of the time/cost/effort].
examples: Old way: 3 copywriters, 2 weeks, $15K. New way: 20 AI agents, 45 minutes, better results. Same script. Fraction of the cost.
Before: 6 hours of manual data entry every Monday. After: 6 seconds. Same data. Zero errors.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Concrete comparison makes the improvement tangible. The specificity makes it credible. The contrast is so stark it creates disbelief → curiosity.
hook_patterns.best_for: Products that dramatically improve on existing processes

hook_patterns.pattern: Lead with credible social proof before introducing the product
hook_patterns.template: [Impressive entity] just [adopted/switched to/built with] [this]. [Why that matters in one line].
examples: The fastest-growing startup in YC's latest batch just rebuilt their entire workflow around this tool. I got them to show me why.
3 of the top 10 YouTube creators switched to this in the last 30 days. None of them were paid to.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Borrowed credibility from known entities. If [impressive group] chose this, it must be worth paying attention to.
hook_patterns.best_for: Products with notable customers or organic adoption

hook_patterns.pattern: Warn about a costly mistake the audience is probably making
hook_patterns.template: The #1 mistake [audience] make with [category] is [specific mistake]. It's costing them [specific cost]. Here's the fix.
examples: The #1 mistake founders make with launch videos is writing the script last. It's costing them 80% of their potential views. Here's the fix.
You're probably making this mistake with your onboarding flow. It's why 67% of your trial users never convert.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Loss aversion is stronger than gain seeking. The viewer needs to check if they're making the mistake. The specific cost makes it urgent.

hook_patterns.pattern: Make a bold prediction about the future of the industry
hook_patterns.template: In [timeframe], [current common practice] will be [obsolete/completely different]. [This] is why.
examples: In 12 months, no serious founder will launch a product without AI-generated scripts. Here's what's already happening.
By 2027, every sales team will use this. The ones who start now will have an unfair advantage.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Creates urgency through future-pacing. The viewer either wants to be early or fears being late. Either way, they watch.
hook_patterns.best_for: Products at the forefront of a trend

hook_patterns.pattern: Take a strong stance that splits the audience
examples: Unpopular opinion: your product doesn't need a better feature set. It needs a better launch video. Here's proof.
Hot take: 90% of SaaS landing pages are actively losing customers. I'll prove it in 60 seconds.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Polarization drives engagement. People who agree share it. People who disagree comment. Everyone watches to see the evidence.

hook_patterns.pattern: Show the transformation with extreme specificity
hook_patterns.template: Before [product]: [painful specific detail]. After [product]: [delightful specific detail]. [Timeframe of change].
examples: Before: spending 4 hours writing launch copy that gets 200 views. After: 45 minutes with AI agents that get 2M views. Same founder. Same product.
Before: our support team answered 400 tickets a day. After: 12. Our customers didn't decrease. Our product got that much better.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: The specificity makes both states vivid. The viewer sees themselves in 'before' and wants to be in 'after.' The timeframe makes it feel achievable.

hook_patterns.pattern: Stack multiple surprising data points rapidly
hook_patterns.template: [Number]. [Number]. [Number]. [What these numbers mean in one line].
examples: 20 agents. 45 minutes. $3M in revenue. Here's the system behind the numbers.
4,000 hours saved. 200 launches. $50M in client revenue. All from one framework.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Rapid-fire data creates an overwhelming impression of scale and credibility. The viewer's brain can't process all three at once — they need to watch to understand.

hook_patterns.pattern: Start in the middle of a pivotal moment
hook_patterns.template: I was [in the middle of something] when [unexpected thing happened]. [One-line consequence]. That's when I [built/found/realized]...
examples: I was reviewing our 47th failed launch video when it hit me: we'd been writing scripts wrong for 10 years. So I built 20 AI agents to fix it.
My client called me at 2 AM. His launch flopped. 200 views. I promised him the next one would hit a million. Here's what we changed.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: In media res drops the viewer into action. The unexpected event creates curiosity. The consequence raises stakes. The reveal promises the solution.
hook_patterns.best_for: Products with a compelling origin story

hook_patterns.pattern: Start with skepticism, then the conversion moment
hook_patterns.template: I thought [product category] was [negative opinion]. Then I saw [specific evidence that changed your mind].
examples: I thought AI-generated scripts were garbage. Then one of our AI scripts outperformed every human-written script in our portfolio.
I told my team to stop wasting time on this tool. A week later, it saved us $200K. Here's what changed my mind.
hook_patterns.why_it_works: Viewers relate to the initial skepticism (they probably share it). The conversion moment creates massive curiosity — what evidence was strong enough to change a skeptic's mind?
hook_patterns.best_for: Products in categories people are skeptical about

anti_patterns.description: Hook patterns that consistently underperform. Avoid these.
patterns: Starting with 'In this video...' — tells the viewer what's coming, closing the curiosity loop before it opens
Starting with a question the viewer can answer with 'no' — 'Want to 10x your revenue?' → 'No' → scroll
Vague superlatives without specifics — 'The most amazing tool ever' means nothing
Starting with your company name — nobody cares who you are yet
Long wind-up before the hook — if the hook doesn't land in the first sentence, it's not a hook
Clickbait that the content can't deliver — breaks trust, kills engagement
Starting with 'So...' or 'Hey guys...' — filler that signals amateur content
